Last night, at two thirteen, the lights in the parking lot flickered.
At two fourteen, the pen moved.
Not much. Just a roll. Like someone had brushed it with a sleeve.
I didn't look at the book. I looked at the camera. On the screen, I was sitting at the des
And behind me, close enough to breathe on my neck, a
man in a wet raincoat was leaning over my shoulder to write.
I didn't turn around. I couldn't.
When the lights came back, the office was empty.
The book was open. The ink was still wet.
Room six. Two fourteen a.m. And the name was mine.
Mr. Pell came in at six. He read the line very quietly.
Then he took a key off the hook. A key I had never seen.
"It's always the one at the desk," he said. "Your room's ready."

places.name: the motel office
places.design: A small, rectangular motel lobby. Walls are dark wood paneling stained a muddy brown. Floor is worn grey-brown linoleum. A long wooden front-desk counter runs along one side, its varnish dulled and scratched. The main objects are: a single green-glass-shaded desk lamp (source of a low, dim, warm amber glow) on the right side of the counter, an open leather-bound guest book centered on the counter, and a brass desk bell to the book's left. A dark window overlooking the lot is behind the counter. A black-and-white CCTV camera is mounted in a high corner. At night, the only light is the desk lamp's amber pool, leaving deep shadows. The weather outside is implied as foggy dark.

places.name: the motel exterior
places.design: Outside: A single-story, L-shaped concrete block motel with a flat overhang roof. The façade is painted a flaking, sun-bleached beige. A row of identical, dark-stained wooden doors, each with a tarnished brass number, lines the building. Interior: The motel office is the only room with a front window lit from within (a warm amber glow). Exterior sources of light are: a single dim yellow bulb above the office door, and one or two tall, flickering sodium light poles in the near-empty asphalt parking lot (casting a sickly, pulsing orange). A two-lane blacktop road runs parallel. Persistent, thick fog hangs in the cold, still night air, swallowing the edges of the lot.
